soundness_flags.label: overlap_constant and ass:cell-overlap
soundness_flags.one_line: Each retained pairwise comparison requires four disjoint cohort-eligibility cells, so p_g1+p_g0+p_c1+p_c0≥4ε; the declared ε∈(0,1/2) permits ε>1/4 and hence an empty law class.

soundness_flags.label: ass:nuisance-estimability and ass:learner-rate-realization
soundness_flags.one_line: Bare common L2 o(n^-1/4) rates do not constitute the cited DML score-regularity condition for the asserted fitted-score L2 and covariance conclusions; add score-stability/Lq control or bounded raw outcome fits.

accepted_scope_caveats.label: thm:joint-system-limit and thm:separate-joint-frontier
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: Optimality is only over constant loadings in the retained finite vector of pairwise DDD scores, not the semiparametric efficiency bound of the full conditional-moment model.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: The headline is joint score-span GMM optimality and its separate-versus-joint frontier under fixed T, retained comparisons, and prespecified aggregate weights.

source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper identifies ATT(g,t) using every clean comparison cohort, permits weights summing to one across those comparisons, and defines the covariance-optimal GMM combination separately for each ATT(g,t).

Theorem 6.3 gives fixed-weight stacked event-study asymptotic normality; Proposition 6.4 includes covariance from shared comparison units; Proposition 6.5 establishes the original-unit-level variance estimator's consistency.

The paper derives efficient influence functions and efficient estimators for overidentified staggered DiD and event-study parameters, including optimal use of comparison groups and periods, but has no DDD eligibility-domain contrast.

source_verification_receipts.locator: Panel-data identification and estimation sections, especially Theorem 5 and the cross-fitting construction
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper supplies canonical panel-DDD identification, an efficient influence-function construction, and cross-fitted nuisance estimation, but not staggered clean-comparison overidentification.

The cited DML theory requires score regularity and refined nuisance-quality conditions; it describes a common L2 o(N^-1/4) rate only as a crude sufficient consequence in smooth problems with those additional controls.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Restrict the common overlap constant to ε≤1/4, or use cell-specific lower bounds whose retained four-cell sum is explicitly below one.
State a DML-compatible score-stability condition—such as uniform L4 control of raw outcome fits plus an L4/L2 propensity-error bound—and derive the fitted-score L2 convergence from it.
After repairing regularity, add a generic compatible-law corollary showing strict gain on an open nondegenerate covariance region, not solely the smallest worked construction.

recommended_next_step: Revise the overlap domain and the DML regularity assumptions, then return this field-tier joint-score-span frontier for Stage 0.
